lots.what_it_is: Victorian style mahogany round breakfast (loo) table, plain round top with moulded edge on a deep frieze, octagonal tapering column, concave triform platform base on bun feet. Possibly a tilt top. Could be 19th century or a later reproduction
lots.guide_summary: No evidence survived: no SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING entries. The researcher found none, and my own WebSearch attempts were refused (session budget of 200 used up). Direct searches on Invaluable, Leonard Joel, Gibson's and Lawsons returned no usable results (empty or 404). The blind $200-500 figure from the scan is unverified.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. Grounds for a closer look (not evidence): the form (faceted column, triform platform on bun feet, deep frieze) fits a William IV or early Victorian breakfast table. In Australia these are often bought as dining tables, but the market for brown furniture is soft. It is pickup only from Moonah with $0 freight, which helps.
lots.confidence_reason: No marks, no price evidence of any kind, and the age and tilt mechanism cannot be confirmed from photos.
lots.dropped_entries: None, as the researcher supplied no entries.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos. The top is a single round board or veneer with good figure and a moulded edge, with light scratches and surface marks and a few small spots. A deep plain frieze that looks veneered, with possible small lifts or chips on the lower edge (photo 2). Octagonal column on a turned collar, concave-sided triform platform on three bun feet, with darker wear on the platform. It looks about 120 cm across, judged by the chairs around it. No label or maker's mark is visible, and the underside and tilt block are not shown. Finish looks like a later polish.
lots.condition: Looks sound and polished, with surface scratches on the top and wear to the base and feet. Not known whether it tilts, whether the column is tight, or whether the veneer is sound underneath.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does the top tilt (with a snap-catch or block) or is it fixed? What is the diameter? Is the column firm with no wobble? Is it 19th century or a reproduction (look under the top for hand-cut screws, pine or cedar blocks and old saw marks)? Any veneer lifts or losses on the frieze or base?

lots.what_it_is: 10 carded Hot Wheels 2023 55th Anniversary matte black and gold series cars: '96 Nissan 180SX Type X, '92 BMW M3, '66 Chevy Nova, '15 Dodge Challenger SRT, '67 Chevy C10, Twin Mill, Mercedes-Benz Unimog U 1300 L (chrome gold chase), Porsche 993 GT2, Custom '01 Acura Integra GSR, '67 Camaro. That is 10 of the 12 in the series, missing the VW T1-GTR (the Mix 1 chase) and the Range Rover Classic
lots.guide_summary: No price evidence survived: no SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING entries. WebSearch was refused (session budget used up), the Hot Wheels fandom page is reference only with no prices, Invaluable gave no results, and hobbyDB and Mighty Ape were blocked for the researcher. The scan's $8-12 per car is unverified.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. These were mainline-priced cars sold in mass retail in 2023. Only the gold Unimog is a chase (1 or 2 per case per the wiki), and it is not a numbered Super. A partial set without the T1-GTR chase limits the appeal of the lot as a set.
lots.confidence_reason: The series and models were read from the card names in the photo and checked against the Hot Wheels wiki series list (fandom API, 1 Oct 2026), but there is no price evidence at all.
lots.dropped_entries: None, as the researcher supplied no entries. Identification corrected: the red car is labelled TWIN MILL on its card, not a 'Lotus-style racer'. The others are the '96 Nissan 180SX Type X (not a Nissan or Honda coupe), '92 BMW M3, '66 Chevy Nova and '15 Dodge Challenger SRT. The series is officially the 55th Anniversary matte black and gold (HLJ96 to HLK08).
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo, 10 cars on blister cards, two of them with 55th Anniversary header cards. All blisters look intact and still on their cards. The card corners and edges cannot be fully seen. The Unimog is chrome gold, the chase. The Twin Mill is red with a gold engine and gold wheels on a TWIN MILL card, but the wiki lists this release as matte black. It could be an unrecorded colour variation, a different release or a swapped car, and this needs checking. Assortment code HDH54 is visible on one header card.
lots.condition: Carded and apparently unopened. Card condition (creases, soft corners, cracked blisters) not visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are there exactly 10 cars, all on their original sealed cards? What condition are the cards in (creases, bent hooks, crushed blisters)? Please check the Twin Mill: is it red on its original sealed card?
